- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7bad6e656a20564f1dff73dedeff7f01e255856` — the merge of head `6946a720608e3b13ff69b5ca967d536cf5ca24df` into base `1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin f7bad6e656a20564f1dff73dedeff7f01e255856 && git checkout f7bad6e656a20564f1dff73dedeff7f01e255856
```

Security-touching: yes

This is the L2 owed by the `Clause-②: yes` line alone. Neither packages/lint nor packages/mcp is a governed path or a spec face, so it carries ①②③ and no ④. I read the net diff `ef39b2c191..e9c4f916b8` and judged the tree; the PR body's account was not taken as evidence. Code I read to judge the scope but did not review: `protocol-data-writes.ts` (`createData` / `updateData`), `protocol.zod.ts` (`CreateDataResponseSchema` / `UpdateDataResponseSchema`), objectql `engine-top-level.ts` (`summaryFieldsLockedOnWrite`, `withSummaryRollUpsReadonly`), `engine-insert.ts` / `engine-update.ts` (the drop listener), lint `authoring-rules.ts` / `runtime-gate.ts` / `finding-user-text.ts`, cli `validate.ts` / `lint.ts`, mcp `mcp-http-tools.ts`.

Security-touching is `yes` for three reasons. The diff teaches the readonly and roll-up write lock: `security.mdx` and the explain entry say who may write a roll-up and that `runAs: 'system'` lifts the lock. It also changes what a write answer reveals about a dropped value. That change is judged under ①, and it reveals nothing new.

Check-runs on the head, read at 10:27Z: 29 success, 16 skipped, 31 in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1-10, Test UI 1-16, Type Check workspace, consumer and UI, Lint lanes, Check Changeset, Build Docs, E2E UI). **None is red.** This verdict assumes the in-progress runs finish green; a red one voids it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **stdio `droppedFields` shape: right.** The member is `DroppedFieldsEvent[]` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, the element type of `CreateDataResponseSchema.droppedFields` and `UpdateDataResponseSchema.droppedFields`. It is collected the way `createData` / `updateData` collect it:
  - the listener pushes each `onFieldsDropped` event as the engine emits it;
  - the member is present only when at least one event arrived (`droppedFieldsMember`, the same `dropped.length > 0 ? { droppedFields } : {}` spread).
  - The engine emits only non-empty `fields`: `emitDrop` / `notifyDrop` return on `fields.length === 0`, and insert gates on `insertDrops.length > 0`. So no `droppedFields: [{ fields: [] }]` can appear.
  - Registering the listener changes no engine verdict. On update, `engineDroppedKeys` is recorded with or without a listener. On insert, the listener is called after the strict refusal.
  - So both transports now answer one engine verdict in one shape. The stdio answer is `unknown` on `McpDataBridge`, and `mcp-http-tools.ts` relays it whole through `textResult`; the stale-roll-up path (`withEarnedAnswer`) carries the member too, as HTTP's does.
- **A clean write answers byte for byte as before: right.**
  - `withoutDroppedKeys(data, [])` returns `data` itself.
  - `droppedFieldsMember([])` spreads `{}`.
  - The key order stays `object, id, record` on both verbs.
- **The `record` change: right, and inside the changeset's sentence.**
  - Create: `{ ...payload minus dropped, ...written }`, so the write result still wins and a dropped key the result leaves out is no longer echoed.
  - Update: `{ ...existing, ...patch minus dropped }`, so a dropped key shows the read-path value. That is the stored value for `readonly`, `readonly_when`, `primary_key` and the roll-up lock.
- **What the answer reveals: nothing new.** `existing` is read with the caller's own context (`findById(engine, object, id, context)`), and before this PR it already filled every key the patch did not cover. The answer now shows a value the caller's read already showed, never a new one. `droppedFields` names only keys the caller itself sent. A `readonly_when` drop tells the caller the predicate held, which the HTTP door already answers the same way.
- **New lint finding `flow-update-summary-field`: right against the engine.**
  - The engine's lock is `type === 'summary' && readonly !== true`, read as `readonly: true` by both static views (`insertStaticReadonlySubject`, `updateStaticReadonlySubject`), with `isSystem` exempt.
  - The branch has the same three properties:
    - it is gated on `!isSystemRun`;
    - it is skipped on a create on an insert-strip-exempt object (the insert subject's own exclusions);
    - it sits after `meta.readonly`, so a declared-readonly roll-up stays the `flow-update-readonly-field` error.
  - On a non-system update of a roll-up that also declares `readonlyWhen`, the roll-up warning is reported instead of the `readonlyWhen` one. That matches the engine, where the static strip takes the key first.
  - `summaryFieldIndex` reads `objectsWithoutTiedFields(objectsAsServed(stack))` through `recordsOf`, which takes both `fields` shapes. Every declared field is in `roIndex` (the `{false, false}` entry), so the `if (!meta) continue` guard does not hide a roll-up.
  - The branch is flow-local, as ruling 7035408057 option B requires: `buildReadonlyIndex` and the hook and action rules are untouched.
- **Barrel export and `os explain` entry: right.** `FLOW_UPDATE_SUMMARY_FIELD` is added to the existing `validate-readonly-flow-writes.js` export block. The explain entry is keyed by its own `rule` string, and its text matches the branch: warning, both verbs, system exempt, platform-object create not judged.
- **Doors the new warning reaches:**
  - The rule runs inside `validateReferenceIntegrity` (`commands: ALL`), so `os build`, `os validate` and `os lint` report it.
  - `os build` has no strict mode, so it passes where it passed. `os validate` and `os lint` pass too, because a warning is never in `errors`.
  - The metadata save and publish doors (`runtime-gate.ts`) put a non-error finding under `advisories`, never in the refusal. That holds on a flow write and on the subject pass of an object write, the one that carries the written package's live flows.
  - `os lint --strict` exits 1, as the changeset says. **`os validate --strict` exits 1 too** ("Treat warnings as errors (exit 1)"; `strictFailing` counts every registry finding that is not `info`). The changeset does not name it, and it does not say that a save or publish answer can now carry the advisory. That is **S1**.

### ② Semver level

- **Bumps: right.** The changeset bumps `@objectstack/mcp: patch` and `@objectstack/lint: patch`, the two packages the diff publishes from. `@objectstack/lint` gains one export and one finding id. `@objectstack/mcp` gains one optional answer member, with no tool input, export or published schema changed. - **`Clause-②: yes`, with no arm: right, on both the changeset body and the PR body.** The surface widens by a new id, an export and an answer member. It is not `(narrowing)`: no build, validate or save that passes today fails, and the strict runs are covered above. Claim amendment 2 (7036853719) corrected the claim's `no` to `yes`, and the tree now carries `yes`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No key, accepted value, metadata type, meaning or default changes for a metadata author. A warning refuses nothing.

- open_question N3 severity: answered by ruling 7035408057, option B. The tree implements B as ruled: warning, its own id, a flow-local index.

- Out of scope, the stdio answers lacking `warnings`, `withheldMentions` and `notice`: answered. The bridge header already lists this as the "spec-shaped receipts" divergence, filed there as the transport-unification follow-up, and this PR does not widen it.

**Dev report 7036824115:**
- Deviation: the file surface widened by two lint files (`index.ts` and `rule-explanations.ts`). Answered by claim amendment 2.
- Deviation: the new warning has no `.user-text.ts` entry. Answered as acceptable, graded **N2** below. `finding-user-text.ts` makes `userTextParams` optional ("a finding without `userTextParams` simply has no user sentence, and its consumer renders `message`"), and the rule's error sibling carries none either.
- Deviation: the PR title was stale. Fixed in round 3; the title now names both halves.

**Dev report 7037040186:**
- Deviation: the round-3 gate list was derived for the changeset path only. Answered as right: `git diff d416d0fd72 e9c4f916b8` touches only `.changeset/35114-stdio-mcp-dropped-fields.md`, and the head's own check-runs carry the full derivation.
- Its other deviations repeat those of 7036824115, answered above.

**SQL push-down:** no finding. The bridge adds no id materialisation, no extra read and no in-app join; `findById` before the update is pre-existing and unchanged. The lint rule is a static walk over metadata.

**Findings:**
- **S1 (should-fix):** the changeset (and the PR body's lint paragraph) name `os lint --strict` as the run the new warning fails. `os validate --strict` also exits 1 on it. The metadata save and publish answers (`advisories`) also gain the finding:
  - on a flow save that writes a roll-up from a user-run node;
  - on an object save that makes a field a roll-up while a live user-run flow of that package writes it.
  - Fix: one clause in the changeset naming `os validate --strict` beside `os lint --strict`, and one naming the save and publish advisory. Prose only; no code change.
- **N1 (nit):** the `withoutDroppedKeys` jsdoc says that for a `stored_expression` key "the write result carries the value the engine stored in its place". That is true on create. On update, the bridge discards the write result, so a dropped `stored_expression` key answers the value read before the update, not the newly computed one. This was never right on this arm: before the PR it answered the caller's own value, and the arm has never read back. The answer is no worse, but the comment overstates it.

- **N3 (nit, L1's):** `security.mdx` says the warning "never blocks a build". That is true for `os build`, but the page omits the `--strict` caveat (S1's two runs).

S1 (should-fix) — the changeset's account of where the new warning bites omits `os validate --strict` and the metadata save/publish `advisories`; it earns a delta review of the prose fix.
